title.narrative: Transformative Leadership Programme for Women in Africa

description.narrative:
The Transformative Leadership Programme for Women in Africa is a one-year initiative led by the Pan-African Catholic Theology and Pastoral Network (PACTPAN) to strengthen women’s leadership within the Church and society across Africa. Although women form the majority of active Church members, they remain underrepresented in decision-making roles due to cultural and structural barriers. The project will train lay and religious women using a train-the-trainer model that promotes sustainability and multiplier impact. The project aimed to further some of the work of SECAM, ACWECA, AMECEA, RECOWA and IMBISA on women leadership in the Church.
Participants will receive practical leadership training in communication, facilitation, advocacy, and decision-making, alongside structured mentorship and networking support. By increasing women’s confidence, visibility, and participation in leadership, the project aims to indirectly benefit over 10,000 community members. The initiative aligns with CAFOD’s commitment to gender justice, participation, and safeguarding, contributing to long-term, locally rooted transformation within the Church and wider society.
